title: Ordinary immersion pullback agrees with quotient-tower completed pullback
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, with $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $u:Y\to X$ be a locally closed immersion of schemes, meaning a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. On $T=X,Y$ put $B_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the canonical coefficient isomorphism $u^{-1}B_X\cong B_Y$ and finite projection identifications [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. Ordinary $Lu^*$ is pullback of modules over these ring sheaves; completed $Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$ and its comparison $Lu^*K\to Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ are the strict quotient-tower construction of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

For every derived-complete $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B_X))$ [def-weil-derived-complete, def-weil-abstract-derived-category] this specified comparison is an isomorphism. Ordinary $Lu^*=u^*$ is exact, preserves derived completeness, and has canonical finite-reduction comparisons $u^*(K\otimes^L_{B_X}(A_n)_X)\cong(u^*K)\otimes^L_{B_Y}(A_n)_Y$ in $D((A_n)_Y)$. These identifications respect quotient transitions, the completion unit and all finite projection maps, including successive quotients. The derived-limit comparison here is the map of strict-tower Roos models induced by the exact, countable-product-preserving inverse image, rather than a choice of a map between unrelated cones. If $K$ belongs to the integral category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], so does $u^*K$, with the same uniform cohomological interval for its reductions.

proof.text: Put $F=u^*$, with scalars transported through the canonical $c_u:u^{-1}B_X\cong B_Y$. The finite projection and transition equations in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image] identify this map with the structure map used in completed pullback, and identify $F((A_n)_X)$ with $(A_n)_Y$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation] with $R=B_X$, $S=B_Y$ and this ring isomorphism: $F$ is additive, exact and preserves countable products. The lemma permits arbitrary schemes and locally closed immersions; no quasi-compactness of the complementary open is required. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], termwise $F$ induces the triangulated derived functor. Exactness identifies it with $Lu^*$: applying $F$ to a quasi-isomorphism from a resolving complex is still a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09AA, lemma-closed-immersion (1); composition with open-slice restriction; coefficient identification as in the cited profinite-coefficient lemma

proof.text: Choose one K-flat representative $P\to K$ with flat terms, and use its strict quotient tower $M_n=P\otimes_{B_X}(A_n)_X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], $FP$ is K-flat with flat terms. The canonical module tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor] therefore gives chain isomorphisms $F(M_n)\cong FP\otimes_{B_Y}(A_n)_Y$, computing the asserted comparisons in $D((A_n)_Y)$. Here the scalar actions are those of Step 1, so these are finite-ring-linear maps, not just maps after forgetting scalars. Naturality of the module tensor comparison for $B_X\to(A_n)_X$ and for every quotient $(A_m)_X\to(A_n)_X$ ($m\ge n$) gives commutative squares with the chain maps $p\mapsto p\otimes1$ and $1_P\otimes\rho_{m,n}$. Hence this is an isomorphism of strict quotient towers together with their maps from the constant tower. In particular it identifies the levelwise pullback tower used in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback].

source.place: Tags 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); sites-modules.tex Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback), naturality in coefficient quotient maps

proof.text: The coefficient pair $(\mathcal O_E,(\varpi))$ is a Noetherian adic coefficient datum in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], so that [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] applies to it: $\mathcal O_E$ is a discrete valuation ring, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]; every $A_n$ is a finite ring [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], so $A_1$ is a finite additive group and in particular torsion; and $A_n$ is perfect over $\mathcal O_E$, resolved by $[\mathcal O_E\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}\mathcal O_E]$ [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect]. The coefficient sheaf of that datum is $B_T$, since the constant sheaf $(A_n)_T$ is also the sheafification of $W\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|W|),A_n)$ [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-coefficient-inverse-image]. First verify invertibility of the actual source completion unit $\eta_K:K\to R\lim M_\bullet$, rather than selecting an arbitrary isomorphism with that target. The coefficient ring is $R=\mathcal O_E$, the ideal is $(\varpi)$, and the quotients are $A_n$ as in the statement. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], quotient-tower completion is canonically Koszul completion, respecting its unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] its value $N=R\lim M_\bullet$ satisfies local derived completeness, and the canonical unit is invertible precisely on locally complete objects. The hypothesis [def-weil-derived-complete] says $K$ is a derived limit of this reduction tower, even though it does not specify a canonical arrow to a fixed model. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-existence], any two such derived limits are isomorphic as objects, so $K\cong N$. Local derived completeness is invariant under isomorphisms, since the vanishing condition on derived internal Hom is; thus $K$ satisfies it. The reflector criterion now proves that this particular $\eta_K$ is an isomorphism. This argument removes the ambiguity about completion units inherent in the triangulated definition. Finally, $K$ lies in the domain of $Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}$: it is derived $(\varpi)$-complete in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. With $r=1$ and $a_1=\varpi$, that definition uses the Koszul tower $Q_m$ of the reflector lemma, and its unit is the chain map $c\mapsto(u_C(c),0)$ into the mapping fibre $F(C)$, whose differential is $(x,y)\mapsto(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. The chain isomorphism $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$ carries $F(C)$ onto the strict Roos complex $\operatorname{Roos}(C\otimes Q_\bullet)$ of [lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison], with differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$. It carries the unit to $c\mapsto(0,u_C(c))$, and $\operatorname{Roos}(u)$ of that is $\eta$ of the component map $C\to L_I$. So the intrinsic unit is the reflector unit, which is an isomorphism because $K$ satisfies the local condition.

source.place: Tags 099B (lemma-derived-completion), 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul); proetale.tex Tag 099M (lemma-naive-completion), with completed-coefficient comparison supplied by the cited equivalence

proof.text: For a strict tower of complexes $M_\bullet$, let $P_M=\prod_nM_n$ and $s_M$ have components $t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. Countable products of modules over $B_X$ and $B_Y$ are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact]. Thus [lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison] identifies $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_M)[-1]$ with the functorial total $R\lim M_\bullet$, respecting every evaluation. Let $\sigma:F(P_M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_nF(M_n)$ be the product comparison from Step 1. For each $n$, $\operatorname{pr}_n\sigma F(s_M)=F(t_n)\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}\sigma$; hence $\sigma F(1-s_M)=(1-s_{FM})\sigma$. The coordinatewise map $(F(y),F(x))\mapsto(\sigma F(y),\sigma F(x))$ is consequently a chain isomorphism between the two Roos complexes: their differentials are $(y,x)\mapsto(-dy-(1-s)x,dx)$, and the displayed equation identifies both coordinates. Combining with the cited evaluation-compatible Roos models gives the specified natural isomorphism $\chi_M:F(R\lim M_\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim F(M_\bullet)$. Each evaluation is the second-coordinate projection, so $e_n\chi_M=F(e_n)$. This is a construction on strict towers, not an arbitrary completion of a triangle morphism.

source.place: Tags 07KC (lemma-products), 08TC (definition-derived-limit); strict evaluation-compatible zigzag as stated in lem-sf-strict-roos-derived-limit-comparison

proof.text: On $P$ the strict quotient maps give the Roos chain map $p\mapsto(0,(p\otimes1)_n)$. Under the strict comparison of Step 4, its image under $F$ is $Fp\mapsto(0,(Fp\otimes1)_n)$, by Step 2 and the defining projection equations for $\sigma$. By the construction in [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], this latter map represents exactly the specified comparison $Lu^*K\to Lu^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$: its constant-tower unit and subsequent strict-tower map have these coordinates in the functorial Roos model. Thus that comparison equals $\chi_M\circ F(\eta_K)$ followed by $R\lim$ of the tower identification of Step 2. It is an isomorphism by Steps 3 and 4. The same equality proves compatibility with the completion unit and every finite projection. For $m\ge n$ the projection square commutes because its components are $1_{FP}\otimes\rho_{m,n}$ on the identified strict towers; the equations for a succession $l\ge m\ge n$ follow from $\rho_{l,n}=\rho_{m,n}\rho_{l,m}$. In particular all successive quotient comparisons agree. Finally the target tower is the quotient tower of $FK$ (Step 2), so this isomorphism identifies $FK$ with its derived limit through its quotient maps. This is derived completeness by [def-weil-derived-complete].

source.place: Tag 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), (2),(5), together with the strict-unit construction in def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback

proof.text: Suppose now $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ as defined in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Its reductions $K_n$ are intrinsically constructible and vanish outside one interval $[r,s]$, independently of $n$. The equivalence [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] identifies this finite-torsion condition with bounded constructible etale origin. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-preserves-bounded-constructible] with $\Lambda=A_n=P_n$ for the adic datum $(\mathcal O_E,(\varpi))$ checked in Step 3, and $g=u$: each $u_n^*K_n$ is bounded constructible and has cohomology in the same $[r,s]$. Applying the origin equivalence on $Y$ gives the intrinsic finite-torsion condition required by the integral definition. By Step 2 these are exactly the reductions of $FK$, and Step 5 gives its derived completeness. Therefore $FK$ belongs to that precise integral category, with the same uniform interval. Only this last paragraph invokes the global finite-torsion coefficient conventions implicit in the integral category; the preceding comparison and completeness argument applied to all derived-complete $B_X$-complexes on arbitrary schemes.
